title: So which RPG Maker is the best

posts.author: Rivratt
posts.body: I've just bought RPG Maker MV(Because it was on sale and i'm not spending 35 on MZ). And i was wondering what engine is best. I'm looking for a Fear and Hunger atheistic. Which one of the many options would be best?

posts.author: Timtrack
posts.body:
Go for MV or MZ, F&H was made with MV and according to rpgLord69
here
, the list of plugins used by the game are listed in the credits.
Older engines are good, but they are less used and you might get less support. Also they are limited in resolution and their tile size is smaller than MV/MZ so you are less likely to find 'new' ressources and scripts for them.

posts.author: ZombieKidzRule
posts.body:
Welcome to the forum!
MV and MZ are very similar with MZ having a few QOL improvements with mapping and it is still being updated occasionally. It also has a few default plugins that I love and use a lot (TextPicture and ButtonPicture).
But pretty much any game you wanted to make in MZ you could make in MV as well. And most tutorials you find will work the same in MV and MZ. And the scripts (javascript) that you can learn to use are the same.
If you already own MV and don't want to spend the money on MZ, you should be able to do what you want to do with MV.
Personally, if you are just starting out with no prior experience with RPG Maker, I'd recommend buying and learning MZ, but that is just my opinion.
Good luck on your projects!

posts.author: Indinera
posts.body: MZ in my opinion mostly because most of Visustella (paid suite of plugins) is accessible and coherent.

posts.author: Ludovinsky
posts.body: Yeah Mv or Mz. If you are new to development just get mv since it's cheaper. Then catch mz on a sale if you really want it. I own every version from xp up. so glad its java and ruby is gone.

posts.author: Piyan Glupak
posts.body:
Both MV and MZ are good. As said above, MZ has a few quality of life improvements, the most useful of which to me is the mapping, which can sometimes make things easier.
MV can deploy to Linux, whereas I understand that MZ can deploy to current Apple devices. MV probably still has a wider range of plugins, often free, or cheaper than the MZ equivalents. (One example of cost is the Yanfly plugin suite for MV compared to the Visustella plugins for MZ.) MV can run on a lower spec machine than MZ, if that is important to you.
Edit - New paragraph inserted here.
If I was going to do another project with a battle party of 6 then I would probably go back to MV, whereas I would otherwise probably use MZ.
There are lots of threads asking similar questions, by the way.

posts.author: Aerosys
posts.body: I have the impression that MZ, both editor and the exported games, just work better with regards of performance. That could be because I like to play on my smartphone or tablet and the touch controls work so much more smoothly in MZ.

posts.author: AquaEcho
posts.body:
Since cost is a concern, MV and its plugins are cheaper (namely Yanfly vs VisuStella), and MV has more (free) plugins overall. MZ plugins are more likely to be pay walled. VisuStella also has a negative performance impact due to its obfuscation and you can't edit its code to adjust to your game. You're also more likely to run into unresolvable plugin conflicts.
MZ has some QoL improvements in its editor, namely the layering in the tile map editor but there are 3rd party tools like the iOS MZ mapper app (that also works with MV) that give you the same functionality.
Aerosys said:
I have the impression that MZ, both editor and the exported games, just work better with regards of performance. That could be because I like to play on my smartphone or tablet and the touch controls work so much more smoothly in MZ.

You can boost MV's performance through upgrading nw.js. I've seen various other hacks here to further improve performance.
There are people who swear by XP being the best though but I've never used it so I can't say. The Pokemon fan game community uses it heavily so it gets a fair amount of 3rd party support through them.
